turn: I finished the "Convert tables" step and committed it as "feat(tables): flatten merged cells". The change is in `src/tables/merged.py`. `expand_spans` now takes a row's (text, colspan) pairs and repeats each cell's text across every column it spans. A merged header like ("Total", 3) therefore becomes three plain cells, and every row ends up the same width. I checked it by tracing a few rows by hand: a row with no merges comes back unchanged, a row with one merged cell widens correctly, and a row that is entirely merged expands to the full table width. I didn't run an automated test suite or exercise rowspans, so vertical merges still need separate handling. In the same commit I also made a small unplanned fix. While reading nearby code I noticed that a leftover unused import in the tables module could trigger lint warnings, and I removed it. Next I will start "Convert code macros".
